findings.exact_quote: the way a bride-to-be is meant to smile at her own betrothal feast
findings.explanation: Cynewise/Cyneric's gender is never fixed, and every other field stays neutral (husband or wife). "Bride-to-be... her" commits to female. The feast is also an alliance feast, not a betrothal feast.
findings.suggested_replacement: the way someone promised in marriage is meant to smile at an alliance feast

findings.exact_quote: What I can tell you is that I never stepped from that bench until the alarm was raised
findings.explanation: Contradicts the same script, where Osric says he poured his own drink and went near the mead-jug once or twice during the toasts.
findings.suggested_replacement: What I can tell you is that I never strayed from my table during that final toast beyond filling my own cup

findings.exact_quote: I have always wondered how a household so careful with its coin still seems to come up short when the accounting is done.
findings.explanation: Osric is the Steward's friend and could not know of the hidden embezzlement. This pre-reveal rumor hints at the murderer's secret and clashes with his trust in the Steward.

findings.exact_quote: my grandfather's grandfather watered cattle on that land
findings.explanation: The family has held the grazing rights for three generations, but a grandfather's grandfather is four or more generations back.
findings.suggested_replacement: my grandfather watered cattle on that land

findings.exact_quote: A steward who guards the ledgers so closely might have more reason than any of us to fear what my sister's sharp eyes could uncover.
findings.explanation: Wulfstan/Wulfhild has no way to know of the Steward's hidden embezzlement. This round-1 rumor points straight at the murderer's secret motive and gives away the solution.
